chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah said:

I said to Hisham ibn Aḥmar: I would like you to ask Aba al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) whether for people who have loans with me that do not demand them from me, is there zakah upon me? He said: 'Do not pay off (the debt) and do not pay zakah, pay zakah.'
As for that which indicates that when the money returns to its owner, zakah is not obligatory upon him until a full year has passed, is what he narrated:

key_terms.قُرُوضاً: Loans (plural of qard, money lent without interest)
key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: A full year passes over it (the lunar year of zakah)
key_terms.يَطْلُبُونَهَا: They demand it (referring to the repayment of the loan)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of zakah on money lent out as a loan (qard) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the narrator asks Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) about zakah on loans (qurūḍ) where borrowers are not yet demanding repayment. The Imam’s concise response, 'Do not pay it off, and do not pay zakah; pay zakah,' is interpreted by scholars to mean that zakah is not due on the loan while it remains outstanding, but becomes obligatory only upon its return to the lender's possession, at which point the lunar year (hawl) begins to count. This clarifies the Shia position that the 'possession' (ḥawl) condition applies to the actual recovery of the debt rather than the initial lending.
